title: CMC 활용 학습에서 면대면 수업, 교사관여 및 메타인지가 학업성취와 상호작용에 미치는 영향

abstracts.value: 본 연구는 전통교실에 비동시적 텍스트 기반 CMC의 효과적인 활용 방안을 알아보기 위해 고등학생 85명을 대상으로 하여 면대면 수업 유무, 교사관여 수준, 학습자의 메타인지가 학업성취와 상호작용에 미치는 영향을 살펴보았다. 본 연구에서 학업성취는 사실적 문제와 일반화 및 추론문제 두 가지로 분류되었고 상호작용은 CMC 메시지를 분석하여 과제관련, 사교적, 절차적 상호작용으로 분류되었다. CMC 과제가 면대면 수업과 관련이 있을 때, 교사 촉진자 상황에서, 메타인지가 높은 학습자의 일반화 및 추론문제 점수가 높았다. CMC 학습과제가 면대면 수업과 관련이 없을 때 사교적 상호작용이 많이 발생하였고 메타인지 상 집단의 과제관련, 사교적, 절차적 상호작용 빈도가 모두 높았다. 그리고 메타인지와 교사관여 수준 사이에 절차적 상호작용 빈도에서 상호작용 효과가 나타났다.

This study examined the effect of face-to-face teaching, teacher-intervention levels(learner-control, teacher-facilitator, teacher-control), and learner's metacognition on academic achievement and interaction to find out effective method of asynchronous text-based CMC use in traditional classrooms. In this study academic achievement was classified into two; the first was factual questions, the second was generalization and inference questions. Interaction was classified into three after CMC messages analysis; task-related, social and procedural interaction. The subjects were 85 students from D High School in D-gun, J province.
The results of the experiment was as follows: First, the generalization and inference question scores were significantly higher with face-to-face teaching than without it. Therefore, we can say it is better to choose learning tasks related face-to-face teaching in learning through CMC.
Second, the teacher-facilitator situation had highest generalization and inference question scores among three teacher-intervention levels. So it is reasonable to assume that teacher's role in CMC is a facilitator, moderator and adviser who provides the framework for learning.
Third, there were many differences in academic achievements and interaction frequencies between upper and lower group in metacognition. For academic achievement, the upper group had better generalization and inference question scores. For interaction, the upper group's social and procedural interaction frequency was higher besides task-related interaction. As metacognition has a strong influences on learning through CMC, it is necessary to have training for improving metacognitive strategies.
Fourth, there were little interaction effects between metacogniton and the other variables. Only procedural interaction frequency had an interaction effect between metacogniton and teacher-intervention levels.
Fifth, face-to-face teaching, teacher-intervention levels, and learner's metacognition had more influence on generalization and inference question achievement than factual question achievement. So learning tasks much more influenced by CMC can be discussion tasks that requires critical consideration and reflection.
